status: MP8 KG1 — first gripper (3D-print pick-and-place from a tray). Purchased-part sizes are public drawings / listings, not measured — verify on arrival. Not printed, not tested.
frame: G: origin = centre of the mounting face (touches the arm tool flange) · +z = approach (away from the arm) · x = jaw travel · y = depth. Parts are modelled in the closed state u = 0 (pad faces touch at x = 0); jaw A opens to -x, jaw B to +x.
decisions: ../../../.dev/mp8-evidence/user-decisions-mp8.json (G1 STS3215 12V · G2 gripper inside 0.5 kg · G3 objects up to 80 mm / 200 g · G4 tray pick · G5 Ø6 rods + printed bores · G6 carbon tube 6 x 4)

fits_from.note: fit values live only in the ledger; writing any of these keys here makes loading stop. When a pending key is judged and moved to the ledger's values, move its name from pending to values here too (README 「다시 만들기」).

servo.source: Feetech C018 page A 45.2 / B 24.7 / C 35 · 55 ± 1 g (quote); Feetech + Waveshare outline drawings (drawing_read: 45.22 × 24.72 · 29 / 32 / 35 layers · spline 10.11 from the output end · spline 3.4 above the 29 face · top holes 18.41 / 39.11 · bottom width spacing 20.5 · horn Ø19.95 (Waveshare 19.2) · horn 4.5 thick · 37.25 over both horns); step boundary 15 and the symmetric 1.5 step are pixel estimates; top-face hole width spacing 20.1 ~ 20.5 (slots); connectors = two 5264 3P on the bottom face about 21 ~ 27 from the output end (pixel estimate) — research 2026-10-28 (.dev/mp8-evidence/research-dims.md)

servo_m2.note: M2 x 5 self-tapping into the servo top holes; head = button / low pan, dia <= 3.8 and height <= 1.6 (the counterbore is Ø4.0 x 1.8) — measure the delivered screws (BOM G06)

pinion_m3.note: M3 x 6 socket head into the horn's tapped flange (2.5) — Waveshare FAQ warns against longer screws

pad_m3.note: M3 x 8 button head (ISO 7380-1 M3: dk 5.7 · k 1.65) — pad B heads sit on the tip side, button keeps them 1.35 below the pad tip

arm_m3.note: M3 socket head (ISO 4762 M3: dk 5.5 · k 3.0) through the base into the arm flange — length set when the arm side is designed

rod.source: user G6 carbon tube 6 x 4; density = pultruded carbon rod listing 1.5 g/cm3 (research) — tube mass about 3.3 g per 140 mm. Tubes go in from the L post (slide fit) through both sleeves and are pressed into the R post only (R-14: no long push through a press hole).

layout.gear_band_note: rack tooth band (both racks); the pinion's front face sits at gear_band_y[1] and its teeth are gear.face_width deep, so the pinion back is 1.0 in front of the rack-A wedge front (y -5) — axial gap 1.0 / 0.65 at horn height 3.0 / 2.65 (review G01 · INT-01)

servo_ledge.note: 45°-ish rib behind the wall under the servo's lower side face (z = z_c - body width / 2): push the servo down onto it while tightening the M2 screws — the slots let the servo float ±0.4 in z otherwise (review G07)

align_groove.note: vertical groove on the base front face (y = base_y[1]) at x = 0 — the pad meeting line must sit on it (± 1 mm) when both jaws are engaged; a 2.4 mm offset means one jaw is a tooth off

gear.note: m1.5 z18 (r 13.5) without profile shift — research: 0.4 nozzle m1.5 ~ 2.0, z >= 17 avoids undercut at 20 deg. Face width 9 + hub 2 (total 11, the horn screws still bite 2.0 into the horn's 2.5 tapped flange) — b 10 -> 9 raises the Lewis stress by 10/9 (review G01). Pinion screw holes = ledger m3_close_hole_dia (the pinion is located on the horn by these four screws — review G07).

pad.grasp_note: pad contact faces span z 58.5 ~ 106 (middle 82.25). Tray pick (G4) puts the pad tips near the tray, so a held object's centre sits at 106 - h/2: 103 = a 6 mm tall object (default, worst for the arm) · 96 = 20 mm · 82.25 = pad middle. Objects taller than 47.5 (106 - 58.5) touch the sleeves when the tips are on the tray (G4 object box check).
pad.screw: M3 x 8 button head (A: through the 3 mm flange into the stalk insert · B: through the 3 mm cap)

fit_coupon.hole_len_note: 8 = the post thickness (press fit grip is judged over the real post length — review R-14)

mesh_jig.note: pinion on a pin between two separate rack bars at the design centre distance: FIT_RACK_A printed flat (teeth in the layer plane like jaw A) · FIT_RACK_B printed standing (teeth across layers like jaw B). The bars slide in x against the outer walls — the pinion drives them like the real jaws.

orientation.JAW_A: y up — the XZ plane on the plate so the rack teeth lie in the layer plane
orientation.JAW_B: z up (as modelled) — rack teeth across layers (rack Lewis Y 0.485 is unverified) · brim on (93.5 tall on a 14.5 deep footprint — review G13)
orientation.PINION: y down — the front face (screw counterbores) on the plate, tooth profile in the layer plane
orientation.KG1_FIT: as modelled — FIT_BLOCK rod holes horizontal like the jaw bores and post holes · M3 holes vertical like the pinion screw holes · FIT_RACK_A flat · FIT_RACK_B standing · FIT_PINION_* y down like PINION
